stop_condition: Every R14 finding is resolved with evidence; the R14-F1 advice-generation fix is verified by an INDEPENDENT reproduction that drives the SHIPPED printed advice literally on both backlog shapes; the R14-F5 --acknowledge-findings design is ruled on with measurements in both directions (false-pass and false-refusal); the full L1 tier is run by QA and reported honestly; and no finding at or above high remains in the release path.

findings.location: .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh:4996-5011 (the R14-TRACK-RECORDED-MAX else-branch) and :5087-5093 (unrecorded_current_advice); comment asserting the claim at :4990-4998
findings.evidence: REPRODUCED, independently, twice, with two different triggers. recorded_max_iter is computed by iterating unrecorded_disk_artifacts -- ON-DISK FILES ONLY -- so a REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 record whose file is not readable on disk is invisible to it, and the R14-F1 branch cannot fire. Trigger A (file deleted): records at iteration=3 and iteration=20, r20's FILE removed, an unrecorded r15 on disk. MEASURED: (1) before any remedy, review-check.sh gate reports ok=true artifact.iteration=20 -- a WORKING selector; (2) approve refuses rc=4 review_artifact_unrecorded and prints 'the highest-iteration listed file, ...-r15.json (iteration=15), is ordinarily the round that should GOVERN this approval -- record THAT one with: qa-gate.sh review-record ... --file ...-r15.json'; (3) following that verbatim yields gate ok=false error_key=review_artifact_selection_disagreement -- the exact R14-F1 defect, on the branch R14-F1 added. Trigger B (no deletion at all): the same shape with r20 present but chmod 000 -- it lands in unrecorded_missing as 'unhashable', contributes to NEITHER max, and the identical wedge results. RECOVERY COST, measured: BEFORE following the advice, the NARROW audited bypass clears it (approve --accept-unrecorded-review 'historic backlog' -> rc=0) and so does the correct remedy (reconcile r15, record nothing -> gate iteration=20, approve rc=0). AFTER following the printed advice, --accept-unrecorded-review is rc=4 review_artifact_selection_disagreement and ONLY --no-review clears it (rc=0, labels=qa-approved) -- writing reviewed_by=none into the approval record of a task that had a valid, attributed, independent review at iteration=20 one command earlier. That is precisely the conflation qa-gate.sh:4900-4906 says must not happen ('folding the two together would force an operator who wants to acknowledge only the backlog to also silently waive findings-resolution they never intended to skip'). Probe transcript: scratchpad probe8-citable.sh / probe9-unreadable.sh, run at HEAD adaf64d + uncommitted change set 09eee6eb.
findings.description: THIRD CONSECUTIVE ROUND for this one advice-generation site (R13-F1, R14-F1, now R15-F1), which is the two-bounce signal: stop patching the comparison and question the assumption all three attempts share. That assumption is stated as fact in the code -- 'this in-loop derivation -- over the exact same on-disk files this refusal already reports on -- is the more robust source, not a second computation of something gate already knows' (:4994-4998). It is not more robust: it answers 'what is the highest iteration among on-disk files whose hash is recorded', while the question the advice must answer is 'what is the highest iteration among RECORDS'. Those differ exactly when a record has no readable file, which is the shape above. REACHABILITY IS CONCRETE IN THIS REPO, not hypothetical: docs/reviews/*-k6re-r13.json and -r14.json are UNTRACKED in git (verified: git ls-files --others --exclude-standard) while their REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 records live durably in the bd store, so any fresh clone, git clean -fdx, or new worktree has records for 13/14 with no files. It does NOT fire on the current working tree (every record there has its file), and firing additionally needs an unrecorded on-disk artifact BELOW 13 -- which is exactly what reconstructing the missing r11/r12 (a known open item on this task: those two rounds left neither file nor record) would create. Fix direction, not prescribed: derive the governing iteration from the RECORD SET rather than the file set -- recorded-hashes already parses iteration= out of every record and could return it alongside the hash -- or, failing that, make the branch conservative when the recorded maximum cannot be established authoritatively, since 'reconcile everything, record nothing' can never invert K3 whereas 'record this one' can.

findings.location: .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh:5088 (the branch-1 advice string) and :4996-5011 (the else-branch that feeds it)
findings.evidence: SAME ROOT CAUSE as R15-F1, opposite branch. The else-branch treats any hash present in recorded-hashes as 'recorded', but recorded-hashes is deliberately the UNION over every record INCLUDING the non-governing REVIEW-ARTIFACT-RECONCILED v1 ones (its own header says so: 'the UNION over every recorded round, never gate's single-winner K3 selection'). So a RECONCILED iteration can become recorded_max_iter. MEASURED: governing record at iteration=3; r20 on disk RECONCILED (non-governing); an unrecorded r5 planted. gate reports artifact.iteration=3. approve's advice prints: 'the round that should GOVERN this approval (iteration=20) is ALREADY recorded ... (MEASURED: gate reports ok:true today for the already-recorded iteration=20)'. gate reports iteration=3, not 20. The advice asserts a specific, wrong gate result and labels it MEASURED. Probe transcript: scratchpad probe7-reconciled.sh.
findings.description: The prescribed ACTION is still safe here (reconciling never changes K3 selection; approve reaches rc=0 afterwards -- verified), so this is a false statement rather than a wedge, which is why it is medium and not high. It is worth fixing with R15-F1 because it is the same one-line conflation and because review-count.test.sh's brand-new Section 15.10 exists precisely to prove that gate distinguishes RECOGNIZED from SELECTABLE -- while cmd_approve's advice, one file away, conflates exactly those two. A refusal envelope that says 'MEASURED' should not be able to contradict the instrument it names.

findings.location: .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh:7596-7603 (ack_marker construction) and :5099 (unrecorded_review_obs, the approve success line); usage text at :2984
findings.evidence: RULING ON THE R14-F5 QUESTION 'can the flag bury a finding'. MEASURED: after review-reconcile --acknowledge-findings over an artifact carrying an unresolved CRITICAL, (a) the durable bd comment does carry '[open findings acknowledged: R1-F1:critical]' -- the claimed protection is real; but (b) review-check.sh gate reports open_findings=0, open_finding_ids=[], observations='independent review; no open findings at/above risk_threshold=high'; (c) recorded-hashes has no field carrying it (keys: count,error_key,hashes,observations,ok,subcommand,task_id); (d) approve succeeds rc=0 and its envelope says, unqualified, 'unrecorded-artifact check PASSED -- all N on-disk review artifact(s) ... are bound by a REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 or REVIEW-ARTIFACT-RECONCILED v1 record (verified by content hash)'. No mechanical reader surfaces the marker; only a human reading the comment stream sees it. Probe transcript: scratchpad probe2-f5.sh P3.1-P3.9.
findings.description: NOT a burial in the sense that matters most: nothing the flag hides was ever visible to gate (gate only counts the GOVERNING record's findings), and before this guard existed the same reconcile happened with NO record at all -- so the guard is a strict improvement and the DESIGN IS RIGHT. Two narrower problems remain. (1) The asymmetry: --accept-unrecorded-review's bypass reason DOES reach the approve envelope and the approval comment via unrecorded_review_obs, while the ack marker does not -- so the one audited escape on this path whose subject is an unresolved CRITICAL is the one that leaves no trace where an approver looks. Carrying the marker into unrecorded_review_obs is a one-line change and would close it. (2) The prose overclaims: qa-gate.sh:2984 says '...so the historic finding is never invisible even though it never governs'. It IS invisible to every programmatic surface. The CHANGELOG ('the comment gains a visible ... marker') and docs/HOOKS.md ('never silently dropped') are both accurate; only the usage text overstates. Given this arc's repeated prose-vs-code findings, fix the word.

findings.location: .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh:7560-7566 (the R14F5-FINDINGS-GUARD rank comparison against the artifact's OWN risk_threshold)
findings.evidence: RULING ON THE R14-F5 QUESTION 'is the self-referential threshold boundary exploitable'. PROBED: an artifact declaring risk_threshold=critical while carrying a high finding reconciles with NO --acknowledge-findings and writes NO marker (rc=0). But the CONTROL settles it: the SAME artifact, recorded so that it GOVERNS, makes review-check.sh gate report open_findings=0 and ok=true. The guard is therefore exactly as strong as the gate, never weaker -- an inflated risk_threshold hides a finding from the release predicate whether or not it is ever reconciled, so this is a pre-existing property of the whole threshold design, not a hole R14-F5 opened. The unreachable-default question is also closed: validate-artifact runs BEFORE the guard and enforces the closed enum on both risk_threshold (ARTIFACT-RISK-THRESHOLD-GUARD, review-check.sh:604-615) and findings[].severity, so the guard's '// 999' and '// 0' fallbacks cannot be reached through the validated path. Probe transcript: scratchpad probe2-f5.sh P4.1-P4.4, P6.1-P6.3 (below-threshold and clean artifacts reconcile with no flag; exactly-at-threshold refuses -- the inclusive boundary is correct and matches gate's own >= rule).
findings.description: NO ACTION. Recorded so the question is answered on the record with a control rather than re-asked in round 16. One observation for whoever extends the tests: sections 8.8/8.9 cover critical-above-high, low-below-high and high-at-high, but not the inflated-threshold shape; adding it as a documented no-refusal case (with the governing control beside it) would make the intended semantics explicit rather than inferable.
